items.q: In a food chain, which organism is the producer?
items.qAf: Watter organisme is die produsent in ’n voedselketting?
items.explain: Producers, such as grass, make their own food by photosynthesis.
items.explainAf: Produsente, soos gras, maak hul eie voedsel deur fotosintese.

items.q: Which organism is a primary consumer?
items.explain: A primary consumer is a herbivore that eats producers, such as a grasshopper eating grass.
items.explainAf: ’n Primêre verbruiker is ’n herbivoor wat produsente eet, soos ’n sprinkaan wat gras eet.

items.q: If all the hawks are removed from a food web, what is most likely to happen?
items.qAf: As al die valke uit ’n voedselweb verwyder word, wat sal waarskynlik gebeur?
items.explain: Removing a predator often lets its prey, such as snakes, increase in number.
items.explainAf: Die verwydering van ’n roofdier laat dikwels sy prooi, soos slange, in getal toeneem.

items.q: Approximately what percentage of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
items.qAf: Ongeveer watter persentasie energie gaan van een trofiese vlak na die volgende?
items.explain: About 10% of the energy passes on; the rest is lost mainly as heat.
items.explainAf: Ongeveer 10% van die energie gaan oor; die res gaan meestal as hitte verlore.

items.q: A plant captures 1000 kJ of energy. About how much energy is available to primary consumers?
items.qAf: ’n Plant vang 1000 kJ energie vas. Hoeveel energie is ongeveer beskikbaar vir primêre verbruikers?
items.explain: About 10% of 1000 kJ is passed on, which is 100 kJ.
items.explainAf: Ongeveer 10% van 1000 kJ word oorgedra, wat 100 kJ is.

items.q: Why are there usually fewer organisms at higher trophic levels?
items.qAf: Waarom is daar gewoonlik minder organismes op hoër trofiese vlakke?
options: Less energy is available to support them
optionsAf: Daar is minder energie beskikbaar om hulle te onderhou
items.explain: Energy is lost at each step, so less energy supports fewer organisms at the top.
items.explainAf: Energie gaan by elke stap verlore, dus ondersteun minder energie minder organismes bo-aan.

items.q: The position an organism occupies in a food chain.
items.qAf: Die posisie wat ’n organisme in ’n voedselketting beklee.

items.q: The place where an organism lives.
A large ecological region with a typical climate and vegetation, such as savanna or fynbos.
items.qAf: ’n Groot ekologiese streek met ’n kenmerkende klimaat en plantegroei, soos savanne of fynbos.

items.q: A relationship in which both organisms benefit.
items.qAf: ’n Verhouding waarin beide organismes voordeel trek.

items.text: A pyramid of [[]] always has a wide base because energy is lost at each level, mainly as [[]].
items.textAf: ’n Piramide van [[]] het altyd ’n wye basis omdat energie by elke vlak verlore gaan, hoofsaaklik as [[]].

items.q: Parasitism is a relationship in which one organism benefits and the other is harmed.
items.qAf: Parasitisme is ’n verhouding waarin een organisme voordeel trek en die ander benadeel word.
items.explain: True. For example, a tick feeding on a dog.
items.explainAf: Waar. Byvoorbeeld, ’n bosluis wat op ’n hond voed.

items.q: Carbon is lost from the biosphere forever when organisms die.
items.qAf: Koolstof gaan vir altyd uit die biosfeer verlore wanneer organismes doodgaan.
items.explain: False. Decomposers release the carbon back as CO₂, so it is recycled in the carbon cycle.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Ontbinders stel die koolstof weer as CO₂ vry, dus word dit in die koolstofsiklus hersirkuleer.

items.q: Producers in an ecosystem contain 20 000 kJ of energy. If 10% passes to each next level, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
items.qAf: Produseerders in ’n ekosisteem bevat 20 000 kJ energie. As 10% na elke volgende vlak oorgaan, hoeveel energie bereik die sekondêre verbruikers?
items.explain: Primary consumers: 10% of 20 000 = 2 000 kJ. Secondary consumers: 10% of 2 000 = 200 kJ.
items.explainAf: Primêre verbruikers: 10% van 20 000 = 2 000 kJ. Sekondêre verbruikers: 10% van 2 000 = 200 kJ.

items.q: Explain why food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels.
items.qAf: Verduidelik waarom voedselkettings selde meer as vier of vyf trofiese vlakke het.
points: Only about 10% of the energy passes to the next level; most is lost as heat, in respiration and in waste.
After a few levels there is too little energy left to support another level of consumers.
pointsAf: Net omtrent 10% van die energie gaan na die volgende vlak oor; die meeste gaan verlore as hitte, in respirasie en in afval.
Ná ’n paar vlakke is daar te min energie oor om nog ’n vlak verbruikers te onderhou.
